Every year, my extended family does a big potluck dinner, and everyone gets assigned something to bring so nobody ends up cooking the whole meal alone.
This year, my aunt sent out a group message with the list, and I was supposed to bring a side dish.
At least, that's what I thought at the time.
I spent the whole afternoon making a big pot of mashed potatoes, and honestly, I was pretty proud of them.
I added extra butter, some garlic, a little cream, the whole thing.
I packed it up carefully, wrapped the pot in a towel to keep it warm, and drove over to my grandma's house, feeling good about myself the entire way there.
When I walked in, my cousin looked at the pot in my hands and just started laughing, almost dropping the plate she was holding.
I had no idea what was so funny.
Then she showed me her phone, and there it was, the actual list.
Turns out, I wasn't supposed to bring a side dish at all.
I was supposed to bring dessert.
Apparently, I'd read the message too fast and just assumed, because that's usually what I bring every single year.
So now there were three side dishes at this potluck and zero desserts, and it was already six o'clock, way too late to go home and bake something from scratch.
My mom tried to be helpful and suggested I just tell everyone the potatoes were dessert.
Nobody found that funny except her.

My uncle, on the other hand, thought the whole thing was hilarious and kept calling my potatoes "the world's saltiest dessert" for the rest of the night, which honestly got old fast, though he clearly wasn't going to stop anytime soon.

My little cousin, who takes food very seriously for a six-year-old, kept walking up to the table and staring at the potatoes like she couldn't quite decide whether they counted as a real dessert or not.
Someone even joked that our family should officially declare potatoes a dessert from now on, just to save everyone the confusion next year.
Honestly, at first I was pretty embarrassed, standing there holding a pot of potatoes nobody had actually asked for.
But then my grandma, who never wastes food, just put them right next to the turkey and said they'd go great together anyway.
And she was right.
People kept coming back for seconds.
By the end of the night, my potatoes were completely gone, and someone actually asked me for the recipe.
My aunt still teases me about it every year now, and she always double-checks with me before sending out the list.
Honestly, I don't even mind.
Bringing the wrong dish turned out to be the thing everyone remembered most about that whole dinner.
